bb56614454.why: The high tell is gone: the stem no longer answers itself, and the key is now the rarity condition, which the stem does not give: if mimics outnumber models, predators learn to target them (Grokipedia, Batesian mimicry). Wrong choices are live and truly wrong ('shun it more', 'never forgetting', and the need-based 'turn foul', M1). Facts: nearly eleven years on the Amazon, foul heliconid models, scarce edible pierid mimics of another family. It now keys a different fact from the kingsnake question in this unit (no model, no protection) and from T1, where mimicry is only a wrong choice.

bc79ee331d.why: The number error is fixed: 'hundreds of plasticine snakes in the Carolinas' (480 there; the 1,200 included Arizona). Choices and key unchanged and true; the context's about 6 percent against about 50 percent are the Carolinas' figures (inside the range against central North Carolina), per ScienceDaily. No new problem.

3bec34166d.why: The self-contradicting 'freeze solid and thaw' choice is replaced by 'It melts tiny ice crystals as soon as they form', truly wrong: antifreeze proteins bind ice and stop its growth while the melting point stays nearly unchanged (Grokipedia), and they even keep the fishes' inner ice from melting in summer (Cziko et al. 2014). Four live choices; key and facts (1961, Wohlschlag, salts about half, the glycoprotein most of the rest) check out. No other unit keys antifreeze.

ff795b5446.why: The grade problem is fixed: the key is no longer basking (grade 3-5) but the cost the lizard's way saves: an ectotherm makes little body heat and needs 10 to 20 times less food than an endotherm (Grokipedia, Ectotherm). The stem no longer names the Sun. Wrong choices truly wrong: lizards digest no more fully than mammals (Karasov et al. 1986); scales do not hold in heat it hardly makes; sunlight only warms it, and its energy still comes from food. 'Runs on sunlight in place of food' contradicts the stem's own point that the lizard still eats, so the key is the one defensible answer. T1 ecosystems' basking turtle (an abiotic factor) and T3 food-web energy are different facts.

e0543e61d3.why: The fangs are gone from the stem ('venom that kills the rodents it bites'), so 'Structural, structural, behavioural' is no longer defensible. Venom is the standard physiological example, ground-coloured blotches structural, ambush behavioural (Kesler TEKS 8.13C guide; Save My Exams). Rattlesnake venom kills prey (Grokipedia). No new problem.

ec630fc91c.why: Facts true: Endler moved guppies from a pike cichlid stream to one with only Rivulus killifish; about 15 generations (two years) later the males were brighter, with larger, more numerous spots; female guppies prefer colourful males (Berkeley; Grokipedia, Guppy). The key is female choice, a general mechanism (a trait spreads because it wins mates, NGSS MS-LS1-4's colourful-plumage example) applied to a new case, not one fish's biology for its own sake; the context adds the general cost-in-one-place idea. No overlap: T2 variation-and-survival keys predators eating the conspicuous beetles; T3 natural-and-artificial-selection keys fitness as leaving the most young (the stag), not mate choice as the selecting agent. The stem names no females or mates; 'males' is needed because only males wear the spots, and the three wrong choices (warning, warmth, startle) stay live.
